prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Houston after a car wreck. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you several specific Houston firms to call and why each is worth contacting — and also what to ask when you call so you pick the best lawyer for your crash. Before I list firms: do you have serious injuries, want a trial-ready lawyer, or prefer a smaller firm that handles a lot of car wreck cases? That would let me tailor recommendations.

A short list to call (good to contact several and compare):

- Mark Lanier / The Lanier Law Firm — well-known Houston trial lawyer with a national reputation. Strong for catastrophic injury or complex liability disputes where you may need an aggressive trial lawyer and extensive resources.

- Arnold & Itkin LLP — Houston-based plaintiffs’ firm with a track record of large verdicts and settlements in serious injury and wrongful-death cases. Good if injuries are severe or liability/causation will be contested.

- Abraham, Watkins, Nichols, Agosto & Aziz (Abraham Watkins) — a long-established Houston personal injury firm that routinely handles car wreck cases and is familiar with local courts, hospitals, and insurers. Good for strong local experience and client-oriented representation.

- Morgan & Morgan (Houston office) — a large national consumer-oriented firm that handles high volumes of auto wreck cases. Good if you want a firm with broad resources, easy intake, and experience with insurance-company tactics.

- Susman Godfrey LLP (Houston office) — a high-end plaintiff litigation boutique that takes major, complex cases to trial. Good when your case has big exposure or commercial/complex legal issues requiring elite litigation skills.

Why call several:
- Different firms have different strengths: big-trial boutiques for catastrophic/complex cases, national firms for consumer access and resources, local firms for hands-on court experience.
- Interviewing several lets you compare approach, fees, estimated timetable, and whether the firm has trial experience with cases like yours.

What to ask when you call (quick script/questions):
1. Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases in Houston? Do you take them on contingency? (If “no contingency,” keep looking.)
2. How many car wreck cases have you handled in the last 2 years? How many went to trial?
3. Do you have experience with injuries like mine (e.g., whiplash, fractures, spinal injury, traumatic brain injury)?
4. Who will handle my file day-to-day — a partner, an associate, paralegal?
5. What is your contingency fee and how are costs handled?
6. Do you advance medical/court/expert costs?
7. What is your estimated timeline and settlement strategy for a case like mine?
8. Can you provide local references or recent verdicts/settlements with case facts?

What to have ready for the call:
- Date/time/location of the wreck, police report number (if available)
- Brief list of injuries and medical care received (ER, hospital, ongoing treatment)
- Photos of vehicle damage, crash scene, injuries
- Insurance information (your carrier and opposing driver’s carrier)
- Any witness contact info

Immediate practical things to do now:
- Get medical care and keep all records/receipts.
- Preserve photos, videos, texting records, dashcam footage.
- Don’t sign medical releases for the other driver’s insurer; you may sign a reasonable release for your own insurer but be cautious with recorded statements.
- Note: Texas statute of limitations for most auto-accident personal-injury claims is 2 years from the crash date, so act promptly.

If you want, tell me:
- the date of the crash, severity of injuries, and whether you already spoke to an insurer — I’ll suggest which of the above firms is best for your specific facts and can draft a short call script you can read on the phone.
